q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Cash-in-Transit' from 'Remittances into Banks' in the railway accounts?

options.A: Cash-in-Transit represents cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised, whereas a balance under Remittances into Banks represents earnings collected but not yet deposited with the bank
options.B: Both the heads represent the cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Cash-in-Transit represents earnings collected but not yet deposited with, or credited by, the bank, whereas a balance under Remittances into Banks represents cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised
options.D: Cash-in-Transit is a suspense head operated for transactions with other Ministries, whereas Remittances into Banks is operated for transactions with the State Governments

e: Cash-in-Transit represents earnings collected but not yet deposited with or credited by the bank. Remittances into Banks represents cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised.

q: The earnings of the Strategic Lines of the Railways for a year are compiled for exhibition in the accounts of the Government of India. These revenue receipts (earnings) are classified under:

options.A: Major Head 1002
options.C: Major Head 3002

e: Revenue receipts of the Railways are classified under Major Head 1001 for Commercial Lines and Major Head 1002 for Strategic Lines, so Strategic Lines earnings fall under 1002.

q: Through-traffic earnings are apportioned among the railways concerned in proportion to the distances travelled over them. The total distance travelled over all the railways is 1,200 km, and the share of earnings falling to Railway Q, over which the traffic travels 480 km, is Rs 7,200. The total through-traffic earnings apportioned are:
e: Railway Q share is 480 / 1200 of the total. So total earnings = Rs 7,200 x 1200 / 480 = Rs 18,000.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Debt Service Fund from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh of the Railways?

options.A: The Debt Service Fund finances safety-related works, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh services the debt obligations of the Railways
options.B: The Debt Service Fund is financed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is credited with appropriations from revenue
options.C: The Debt Service Fund is credited with appropriations made from the revenues of the Railways and is intended to provide a cushion for meeting the Railways' debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, created in the Budget for 2017-18, finances safety-related works, including the renewal and replacement of safety assets
options.D: Both the funds were created in the Budget for 2017-18 with an identical corpus

e: The Debt Service Fund is credited with appropriations from railway revenues as a cushion for debt-service obligations in lean years. The RRSK, created in 2017-18, finances safety works including renewal of safety assets.

q: While the Special Railway Safety Fund was in existence, it was maintained in the Public Account of India. A clerk proposes to exhibit the Fund in the Government accounts under Major Head 8009. The correct Major Head for the Fund was:

options.A: Major Head 8009
options.C: Major Head 8230

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund, held in the Public Account, was exhibited under Major Head 8230. Major Head 8009 relates to State Provident Funds and 8443 to Civil Deposits.

q: The capital expenditure of the Government for a year is Rs 5,20,000 crore, and the grants-in-aid given during the year for the creation of capital assets are Rs 85,000 crore. The Effective Capital Expenditure of the Government for the year, as shown in the Budget documents, is:

options.A: Rs 6,05,000 crore
options.C: Rs 5,20,000 crore

e: Effective Capital Expenditure = capital expenditure + grants for capital assets = Rs 5,20,000 crore + Rs 85,000 crore = Rs 6,05,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'token grant' from an 'Exceptional Grant' voted by Parliament?

options.A: A token grant is a grant for a purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year, whereas an Exceptional Grant is a nominal grant for a new service
options.B: A token grant is a nominal amount voted to obtain the approval of Parliament for a new service which is financed by re-appropriation of savings within the grant, whereas an Exceptional Grant is a grant made under Article 116 for a purpose which forms no part of the current service of any financial year
options.C: Both the grants are voted only after the close of the financial year to regularise excess expenditure
options.D: A token grant is voted by the Rajya Sabha, whereas an Exceptional Grant is voted by the Lok Sabha

e: A token grant is a nominal amount voted for a new service financed by re-appropriation within the grant. An Exceptional Grant under Article 116 is for a purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year.

q: The Railway Convention Committee is required to be constituted for reviewing the financial relationship between the Railways and the General Finances. The Committee is constituted:

options.A: By the President under Article 263 of the Constitution
options.B: By the Railway Board through an office order
options.C: By the Finance Commission along with its report
options.D: On a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha

e: The Railway Convention Committee is constituted on a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha, to review the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances.

q: Of the assured annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, the amount met from Gross Budgetary Support is Rs 15,000 crore. The share of the annual outlay met from the internal resources of the Railways, expressed as a percentage of the assured outlay, is:

options.A: 75 per cent
options.C: 20 per cent

e:
Internal resources share = Rs 20,000 crore - Rs 15,000 crore = Rs 5,000 crore, which is Rs 5,000 / Rs 20,000 x 100 = 25 per cent of the assured RRSK outlay.
Update: the figures in this question describe the original RRSK design (assured outlay Rs 20,000 crore a year: Rs 15,000 crore GBS + Rs 5,000 crore internal resources). RRSK's currency has since been extended for a further five years w.e.f. 2022-23, with total Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 45,000 crore. (Source: Ministry of Railways, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 138, answered 02.02.2024.)

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the principle of 'unity' in Government budgeting from the principle of 'annuality'?

options.A: Unity requires that the authorisation of Parliament be valid for one financial year only, whereas annuality requires that all receipts and expenditure be presented in a single budget
options.B: Unity and annuality are two names for the same principle of budgeting
options.C: Unity requires that all the receipts and expenditure of the Government be presented together in a single unified budget, whereas annuality means that the authorisation of Parliament to incur expenditure is valid for one financial year only
options.D: Unity applies only to the Railway Budget, whereas annuality applies only to the General Budget

e: Unity requires all receipts and expenditure to be presented together in a single unified budget. Annuality means Parliament authorisation to incur expenditure is valid for one financial year only.

q: A newly nominated member of the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways asks when the system of such committees, which examine the Demands for Grants of the Ministries, was set up. The Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament were set up in the year:
e: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees, which examine the Demands for Grants of the Ministries, were set up in 1993.

q: The corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund was Rs 17,000 crore. Of this corpus, a contribution of about Rs 5,000 crore was raised by the Railways mainly through a safety surcharge levied on passenger fares. The balance of the corpus, provided from the General Finances, was:

options.A: Rs 11,000 crore
options.C: Rs 13,000 crore

e: Balance from General Finances = corpus - railway contribution = Rs 17,000 crore - Rs 5,000 crore = Rs 12,000 crore for the Special Railway Safety Fund.

q: A report of the Estimates Committee of Parliament, examining the estimates of the Ministry of Railways, is ready for presentation. The report is presented to:

options.A: The Lok Sabha only
options.C: Both Houses of Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee consists of members of the Lok Sabha only, and its reports are presented to the Lok Sabha only.

q: The gross earnings of a zonal railway for a year are Rs 8,400 crore and its Operating Ratio for the year is 95 per cent. The net revenue (surplus) of the railway for the year is:

options.A: Rs 380 crore
options.C: Rs 420 crore

e: Working expenses = 95 per cent of Rs 8,400 crore = Rs 7,980 crore. Net revenue = Rs 8,400 crore - Rs 7,980 crore = Rs 420 crore.

q: The surplus (net revenue) of the Railways for a year has been worked out after the close of the financial year. The appropriations to be made out of this surplus to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund are determined:

options.A: In the Budget Estimates, as a fixed percentage of the gross earnings
options.B: By the Railway Convention Committee, once in five years
options.C: Monthly, in equal instalments throughout the year
options.D: At the close of the financial year, with reference to the actual surplus (net revenue) available for the year

e: Appropriations out of surplus to the Development Fund and Capital Fund are made at the close of the financial year, with reference to the actual surplus or net revenue available for that year.

q: In a year governed by the Separation Convention, a zonal compilation shows that the Railways earned a net revenue, but the amount was not enough to discharge the entire dividend payable to General Revenues for that year. The portion of the dividend which remained unpaid in these circumstances was carried to the:

options.A: Deferred Dividend Liability Account
options.C: Contingency Fund of India

e: Under the Separation Convention, if net revenue was insufficient to pay the full dividend to General Revenues, the unpaid portion was carried to the Deferred Dividend Liability Account.

q: A new railway line is still under construction and has not been opened for public traffic. During construction, the line earns some net earnings from the carriage of construction material and other traffic. These net earnings are:

options.A: Credited to the revenue earnings of the year
options.C: Credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of its cost
options.D: Treated as Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways

e: Net earnings of a line still under construction, from carriage of construction material and other traffic, are credited to the Capital account of the work in reduction of its cost, as the line is not yet open for public traffic.

q: A major bridge work, financed partly out of borrowed capital, remains under construction for three years before it is opened for traffic. The interest accruing on the borrowed capital during this construction period is, in the railway accounts:

options.A: Charged to the working expenses of the year
options.B: Treated as part of the cost of the work and charged to Capital
options.C: Debited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Ignored in the accounts till the work is opened for traffic

e: Interest on borrowed capital during the construction period, before a work is opened for traffic, is treated as part of the cost of the work and charged to Capital.

q: An Accounts Officer proposes to effect a re-appropriation of funds within a grant entirely on the orders of the executive authority, without any other concurrence. The correct position is that orders of re-appropriation within a grant are issued by the competent authority with the concurrence of:

options.A: The statutory Audit office
options.B: The executive department alone, without any finance concurrence
options.C: The Railway Board in every case

e: Re-appropriation of funds within a grant is ordered by the competent authority only with the concurrence of the associated Finance and Accounts branch; executive orders alone are not sufficient.

q: The actual expenditure under a Demand exceeds the allotment under one Sub-Major Head, though the total amount of the Grant is not exceeded. For the purposes of the Appropriation Accounts and the regularisation of excess expenditure, the excess or saving under the Demand is reckoned with reference to:

options.A: Each Primary Unit separately
options.B: The total amount of the Grant (Demand) as a whole
options.C: Each individual work separately

e: For Appropriation Accounts, excess or saving is reckoned with reference to the total amount of the Grant or Demand as a whole, not separately for each Sub-Major Head, Primary Unit or work.

q: Additional funds are required by the Ministry of Railways during the course of a financial year and Supplementary Demands for Grants are prepared. Unlike the main Demands presented with the Budget, the Supplementary Demands are:

options.A: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before they are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees
options.D: Presented only during the Budget Session of Parliament

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees, unlike the main Demands presented with the Budget.

q: In the printed Demands for Grants, an Accounts Officer has to identify the items of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, as distinct from the voted expenditure. The charged expenditure is distinguished in the Budget documents by being:

options.A: Printed in italics
options.B: Shown in a separate Demand altogether
options.C: Marked with an asterisk against each item

e: In the printed Demands for Grants, expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is distinguished from voted expenditure by being printed in italics.

q: A deposit work is executed by a zonal railway for an outside party, the cost being met from the amount deposited by the party. The work is proposed to be included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) of the railway. The correct position is that deposit works:

options.A: Are shown as itemised works in the Pink Book
options.B: Do not form part of the Railways' Works Programme (Pink Book), their cost being met from the amounts deposited by the parties concerned
options.C: Are financed out of the Development Fund and shown in the Pink Book
options.D: Require a separate Demand for Grant in the Railway Budget

e: Deposit works are financed from amounts deposited by the parties concerned and do not form part of the Railways Works Programme in the Pink Book, which covers works financed from railway funds and Capital.

q: At the close of a financial year, considerable balances remain outstanding under the suspense and remittance heads in the books of a zonal railway, pending clearance to the final heads. These balances:

options.A: Lapse to the Government at the close of the year
options.B: Are written off automatically at the close of the year
options.C: Are transferred to the Capital Fund of the Railways
options.D: Are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance

e: Balances under suspense and remittance heads do not lapse at the close of the year. They are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance to the final heads of account.

q: An Accounts Officer, new to budget work, proceeds on the assumption that Supplementary Demands for Grants can be presented to Parliament in only one batch during a financial year. The correct position is that Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented during the course of a financial year in:

options.A: One batch only
options.C: Three batches

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented during a financial year in three batches, and not in only one batch.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Depreciation Reserve Fund from the Railway Safety Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares, whereas the Railway Safety Fund is credited with appropriations from revenue assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of assets
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited with appropriations from revenue, assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of assets, for the renewal and replacement of railway assets, whereas the Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and is used mainly for works relating to level crossings and road over and under bridges
options.C: Both the funds are credited with appropriations made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways at the close of the financial year
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund finances works of passenger amenities, whereas the Railway Safety Fund finances the renewal and replacement of assets generally

e: The DRF is credited with revenue appropriations based on original cost and codal life for renewal and replacement. The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge on fares and used mainly for level crossing and road bridge works.

q: The gross earnings of a zonal railway for a year are Rs 9,600 crore and its net revenue (surplus) for the year is Rs 480 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway for the year is:

options.A: 90 per cent
options.C: 95 per cent

e: Working expenses = Rs 9,600 crore - Rs 480 crore = Rs 9,120 crore. Operating Ratio = Rs 9,120 / Rs 9,600 x 100 = 95 per cent.

q: A station has booked traffic during the last week of March, but the cash for a part of the traffic is collected only in April. A clerk proposes to bring the earnings to account only when the cash is actually collected. The correct position is that the earnings of the Railways are brought to account:

options.A: On the basis of the traffic booked, irrespective of when the cash is collected
options.B: Only on the basis of the cash actually collected and remitted during the financial year
options.C: Partly on the booked basis and partly on the cash basis, at the option of the zonal railway
options.D: Only after the Traffic Book for the year has been finally closed

e: Railway earnings are brought to account on the basis of traffic booked, on an accrual basis, irrespective of when the cash for the booked traffic is actually collected.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year works out to Rs 1,470 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 85 crore was obtained under the Demand and funds of Rs 55 crore were surrendered out of it. The original grant under the Demand was:

options.A: Rs 1,610 crore
options.C: Rs 1,500 crore

e: Final Grant = original grant + supplementary grant - surrenders. So original grant = Rs 1,470 crore - Rs 85 crore + Rs 55 crore = Rs 1,440 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'debt heads' from 'suspense heads' in railway accounts?

options.A: Debt heads record transactions representing definite liabilities of the Government, or amounts recoverable by it, such as deposits and provident fund balances, whereas suspense heads record transactions only temporarily, pending their adjustment to the final heads of account concerned
options.B: Debt heads record transactions only temporarily pending adjustment, whereas suspense heads record the definite liabilities of the Government
options.C: Debt heads are operated only for transactions with the Reserve Bank of India, whereas suspense heads are operated only for transactions with State Governments
options.D: Debt heads and suspense heads are two names for the same group of heads in the classification of accounts

e: Debt heads record definite liabilities of Government or amounts recoverable by it, such as deposits and provident fund. Suspense heads record transactions temporarily, pending adjustment to the final heads concerned.

q: Reservation fees and superfast supplementary charges collected from passengers by a zonal railway are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings
options.C: Goods Earnings

e: Reservation fees and superfast supplementary charges are part of the fare-related coaching receipts and are classified under Passenger or Coaching Earnings, not under Sundry Other Earnings or Goods Earnings.

q: The opening credit balance under the 'Deposits' head of a railway is Rs 3,90,000. During the year, deposits of Rs 9,85,000 are repaid or adjusted and debited to the head, and the closing credit balance under the head is Rs 6,55,000. The deposits received and credited to the head during the year amount to:
e: Deposits received = closing balance + repaid - opening balance = Rs 6,55,000 + Rs 9,85,000 - Rs 3,90,000 = Rs 12,50,000.

q: A Demand for Grant is put to the vote of the Lok Sabha and is passed by the House. On being so passed, the Demand becomes:

options.A: An Appropriation
options.C: A Vote on Account

e: A Demand for Grant, when voted and passed by the Lok Sabha, becomes a Grant. It becomes an Appropriation only through the Appropriation Act that follows.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Journal Book' from the 'Trial Balance' in the books of a railway?

options.A: The Journal Book is a statement of the balances of the Ledger accounts, whereas the Trial Balance is the book in which transfer entries are first recorded
options.B: The Journal Book is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Trial Balance is rendered monthly to the Railway Board
options.C: The Journal Book is the book of original entry in which all transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded, whereas the Trial Balance is a statement of the balances of the Ledger accounts, prepared to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books
options.D: The Journal Book and the Trial Balance are two names for the same record maintained in the Accounts Office

e: The Journal Book is the book of original entry where transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded. The Trial Balance is a statement of Ledger balances prepared to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books.

q: The Block Account of a railway at the close of a year stands at Rs 61,400 crore. The capital outlay incurred during the year is Rs 4,200 crore and assets of the original cost of Rs 650 crore were sold and removed from the Block during the year. The Block Account at the commencement of the year stood at:

options.A: Rs 64,950 crore
options.C: Rs 57,200 crore

e: Opening Block = closing Block - capital outlay + assets removed = Rs 61,400 crore - Rs 4,200 crore + Rs 650 crore = Rs 57,850 crore.

q: A clerk in the Accounts Office, while preparing a note on the parliamentary committees, records that the Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament was first constituted in the year 1950. The correct position is that the Committee was first constituted in the year:
e: The Committee on Public Undertakings was first constituted in 1964, not in 1950. The Estimates Committee dates to 1950 and the Public Accounts Committee to 1921.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Revenue Budget from the Capital Budget of the Railways?

options.A: The Revenue Budget covers the annual plan outlay and its financing, whereas the Capital Budget covers the earnings and working expenses of the Railways
options.B: The Revenue Budget is presented only to the Rajya Sabha, whereas the Capital Budget is presented only to the Lok Sabha
options.C: Both the budgets cover only the working expenses of the Railways, the Revenue Budget in detail and the Capital Budget in summary
options.D: The Revenue Budget covers the earnings and working expenses of the Railways, whereas the Capital Budget covers the annual plan outlay of the Railways and its financing through Gross Budgetary Support, internal resources and Extra Budgetary Resources

e: The Revenue Budget covers earnings and working expenses of the Railways. The Capital Budget covers the annual plan outlay and its financing through Gross Budgetary Support, internal resources and Extra Budgetary Resources.

q: The closing debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' of a railway is Rs 290 lakh. During the year, stores of Rs 980 lakh are received into stock and stores of Rs 1,060 lakh are issued from stock. The opening debit balance under the head was:

options.A: Rs 370 lakh
options.C: Rs 450 lakh

e: Opening balance = closing balance - stores received + stores issued = Rs 290 lakh - Rs 980 lakh + Rs 1,060 lakh = Rs 370 lakh under Stores Suspense.

q: The Finance Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha immediately after the presentation of the Budget, is taken up by the House for consideration and passing:

options.A: Immediately after its introduction, before the general discussion on the Budget
options.B: After the Appropriation Bill has been passed
options.C: Before the Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha
options.D: Only in the session following the Budget Session

e: The Finance Bill is taken up for consideration and passing only after the Demands for Grants are voted and the Appropriation Bill has been passed.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Reserve Bank Suspense' from 'AG Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: Reserve Bank Suspense is operated for adjustments with State Governments pending settlement, whereas AG Suspense is operated for transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: Both the heads are operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, pending receipt of the bank's advice
options.C: Reserve Bank Suspense represents transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank of India, pending the Bank's advice, whereas AG Suspense is operated for adjustments of transactions between the Railways and the State Governments and Accountants General, pending settlement
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense represents the cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank, whereas AG Suspense represents cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank

e: Reserve Bank Suspense covers transactions in course of settlement with the RBI pending its advice. AG Suspense covers adjustments between the Railways and State Governments and Accountants General pending settlement.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year is Rs 780 crore and the actual expenditure booked against the Demand exceeds the Final Grant by Rs 45 crore. The actual expenditure booked against the Demand is:

options.A: Rs 825 crore
options.C: Rs 780 crore

e: Actual expenditure = Final Grant + excess over Final Grant = Rs 780 crore + Rs 45 crore = Rs 825 crore.

q: An Accounts Officer proposes to furnish explanations in the Appropriation Accounts for every variation, however small, between the Final Grant and the actual expenditure under a Demand. The correct position is that explanations for such variations are required to be furnished:

options.A: For every variation, without any exception
options.B: Only for variations under the charged portion of the Grant
options.C: Only where the variation is pointed out by the statutory Audit office
options.D: For variations which exceed the prescribed limits

e: In the Appropriation Accounts, explanations for variations between Final Grant and actual expenditure are required only for variations which exceed the prescribed limits, not for every small variation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Small Savings Fund from the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund of the Government of India?

options.A: The National Small Savings Fund is financed mainly by a cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is credited with the collections under the small savings schemes
options.B: The National Small Savings Fund, maintained in the Public Account of India, is credited with the collections under the small savings schemes and its balances are invested in Central and State Government securities, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is financed mainly by a cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel
options.C: Both the funds are maintained in the Consolidated Fund of India and are credited with the proceeds of disinvestment
options.D: The National Small Savings Fund was created out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund forms part of the Public Account of India

e: The National Small Savings Fund in the Public Account is credited with small savings collections, invested in Central and State securities. The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is financed mainly by cess on petrol and high speed diesel.

q: The opening debit balance under the suspense head 'Miscellaneous Advances' of a railway is Rs 3,60,000. During the year, advances of Rs 10,20,000 are made and debited to the head, and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 4,45,000. The advances recovered or adjusted and credited to the head during the year amount to:
e: Recovered = opening balance + advances made - closing balance = Rs 3,60,000 + Rs 10,20,000 - Rs 4,45,000 = Rs 9,35,000.

q: Demurrage and wharfage charges recovered by a zonal railway from traders are proposed by a clerk to be credited to Sundry Other Earnings. The correct classification of wharfage charges in the railway accounts is under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Demurrage and wharfage charges are charges connected with goods traffic and detention of wagons and goods, and are classified under Goods Earnings in railway accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the March (Preliminary) Account Current from the March (Final) Account Current of a zonal railway?

options.A: The March (Preliminary) Account Current is rendered by the Railway Board to the zonal railways, whereas the March (Final) Account Current is rendered by the zonal railways to the Railway Board
options.B: The March (Preliminary) Account Current covers only the cash transactions of March, whereas the March (Final) Account Current covers only the transfer transactions of the year
options.C: The March (Preliminary) Account Current is the first rendering of the account for March, whereas the March (Final) Account Current is rendered thereafter to incorporate the adjustments and corrections received after the rendering of the Preliminary account, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly
options.D: The March (Preliminary) Account Current is audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the March (Final) Account Current is not audited

e: The March Preliminary Account Current is the first rendering for March. The March Final Account Current follows it to incorporate adjustments and corrections received later, so the year accounts close completely and correctly.

q: At a surprise check of an imprest, the cash in hand with the holder is Rs 4,800 and the paid vouchers held by him in support of the expenditure incurred out of the imprest, and not yet recouped, amount to Rs 11,700. The sanctioned amount of the imprest is:
e: Imprest amount = cash in hand + paid vouchers not yet recouped = Rs 4,800 + Rs 11,700 = Rs 16,500.

q: Along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants for a year, supplementary estimates for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India are also presented to the Lok Sabha. In the House, these charged supplementary estimates are:

options.A: Not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha, like all charged expenditure
options.B: Voted by the Lok Sabha in the same manner as the Supplementary Demands
options.C: Examined and voted by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Approved by the Public Accounts Committee before presentation

e: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha. This applies equally to supplementary estimates for charged expenditure.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Transfer Entry Order' from a 'Journal Voucher' in railway accounts?

options.A: A Transfer Entry Order supports the cash entries in the Main Cash Book, whereas a Journal Voucher authorises every transfer adjustment between two railways
options.B: A Transfer Entry Order is issued by the Reserve Bank of India, whereas a Journal Voucher is issued by the Railway Board
options.C: Both the documents are issued by the executive departments and neither requires the signature of an Accounts Officer
options.D: A transfer (journal) adjustment in the railway accounts is authorised and recorded through a Transfer Entry Order, whereas a Journal Voucher is the voucher supporting the entries in the Journal Book, duly signed by an Accounts Officer

e: A transfer or journal adjustment is authorised and recorded through a Transfer Entry Order. A Journal Voucher is the voucher supporting entries in the Journal Book, duly signed by an Accounts Officer.

q: The closing balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense' of a railway, representing the cost of jobs in progress in its workshops, is Rs 65 lakh. During the year, jobs of Rs 440 lakh are charged to the head and completed jobs of Rs 475 lakh are transferred out of it. The opening balance under the head was:

options.A: Rs 30 lakh
options.C: Rs 100 lakh

e: Opening balance = closing balance - jobs charged + jobs transferred out = Rs 65 lakh - Rs 440 lakh + Rs 475 lakh = Rs 100 lakh under Manufacturing Suspense.

q: A clerk records that the Separation Convention of 1924, which separated the finances of the Railways from the general finances of the Government of India, was given effect to through an Act of Parliament. The correct position is that the Convention was given effect to through:

options.A: A resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly
options.B: An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor-General
options.C: A resolution adopted by the Railway Board

e: The Separation Convention of 1924 was not enacted by any Act or Ordinance: it was given effect through a resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly in September 1924, separating railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India from 1924-25.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Single Account Current' now rendered by a zonal railway from the 'Approximate Account Current' rendered under the earlier practice?

options.A: Under the earlier practice, an Approximate Account Current, giving approximate figures, was rendered first and was followed by a final Account Current, whereas a zonal railway now renders a single monthly Account Current in place of that two-stage practice
options.B: The Single Account Current is rendered only once a year, whereas the Approximate Account Current was rendered every month
options.C: The Single Account Current covers only the transfer transactions of the month, whereas the Approximate Account Current covered only the cash transactions
options.D: There is no difference between the two, the Single Account Current being only a new name for the Approximate Account Current

e: Under the earlier practice an Approximate Account Current with approximate figures was rendered first, followed by a final Account Current. A zonal railway now renders a single monthly Account Current in place of that two-stage practice.

q: The primary deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 4,20,000 crore and its interest payments during the year amount to Rs 3,80,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 40,000 crore
options.C: Rs 8,40,000 crore

e: Fiscal deficit = primary deficit + interest payments = Rs 4,20,000 crore + Rs 3,80,000 crore = Rs 8,00,000 crore.

q: Stores are issued from a stores depot of a zonal railway to a revenue work of the railway. In the railway accounts, the value of the stores so issued is credited to:

options.A: The head of account of the revenue work concerned
options.C: Stores Suspense

e: Stores issued from stock to a work are credited to Stores Suspense, which is debited when stores are received into stock, so the stock account reflects the issue correctly.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Gross Budgetary Support from Extra Budgetary Resources in the financing of the Railways' annual plan outlay?

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support is the budgetary support extended to the Railways through the Union Budget, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways
options.B: Gross Budgetary Support is raised from the market through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources are provided through the Union Budget
options.C: Both Gross Budgetary Support and Extra Budgetary Resources form part of the internal resources of the Railways
options.D: Gross Budgetary Support is met out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources are met out of the balances of the Railway Funds

e: Gross Budgetary Support is support extended through the Union Budget. Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market, and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways.

q: The opening debit balance under the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' of a railway is Rs 1,10,000. During the month, the bank gives credit for remittances of Rs 13,90,000 and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 85,000. The remittances made into the bank during the month amount to:
e: Remittances made = closing balance + bank credit - opening balance = Rs 85,000 + Rs 13,90,000 - Rs 1,10,000 = Rs 13,65,000.

q: A member of the Lok Sabha demands that the estimates of the receipts of the Government, as presented in the Annual Financial Statement, also be put to the vote of the House along with the Demands for Grants. The correct position is that the estimates of receipts are:

options.A: Voted by the Lok Sabha after the Demands for Grants are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Voted jointly by both Houses of Parliament
options.D: Not subjected to a vote of Parliament; it is only the Demands for Grants for expenditure that are voted by the Lok Sabha

e: Estimates of receipts in the Annual Financial Statement are not voted by Parliament. Only the Demands for Grants for expenditure are voted by the Lok Sabha.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Expenditure Profile' from 'Budget at a Glance'?

options.A: The Expenditure Profile presents a brief summary of the Budget showing the deficit indicators, whereas Budget at a Glance presents a ministry-wise snapshot of the total expenditure of the Government
options.B: The Expenditure Profile mainly presents a snapshot, or broad overview, of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise, whereas Budget at a Glance presents a brief summary of the Budget, showing the receipts, expenditure and the various deficit indicators
options.C: Both the documents present only the detailed head-wise estimates of expenditure of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: The Expenditure Profile is presented only in an election year, whereas Budget at a Glance is presented every year

e: The Expenditure Profile gives a ministry-wise and scheme-wise snapshot of the pattern of total expenditure. Budget at a Glance gives a brief summary of receipts, expenditure and deficit indicators.

q: The earnings apportioned to a zonal railway for a period, after apportionment of through-traffic earnings, are Rs 5,150 crore, and the railway records a net gain of Rs 350 crore on apportionment for the period. The earnings originated and collected by the railway for the period are:

options.A: Rs 4,800 crore
options.C: Rs 4,650 crore

e: Apportioned earnings = originated earnings + gain on apportionment. So originated earnings = Rs 5,150 crore - Rs 350 crore = Rs 4,800 crore.

q: A clerk preparing the Detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways proposes to exhibit, for each head of account, only the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year. The correct position is that the Detailed Demands for Grants exhibit, for each head of account, the figures relating to:

options.A: The Budget Estimates of the ensuing year only
options.B: The Actuals of the preceding year and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year only
options.C: The Actuals of the preceding year, the Budget Estimates and the Revised Estimates of the current year, and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year
options.D: The Revised Estimates of the current year and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year only

e: Detailed Demands for Grants show for each head the Actuals of the preceding year, the Budget and Revised Estimates of the current year, and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Safety Fund from the Capital Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Railway Safety Fund is credited with appropriations made out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas the Capital Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.B: Both the funds are credited with appropriations from revenue assessed on an actuarial basis
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund finances the creation of new assets generally, whereas the Capital Fund is used only for works relating to level crossings
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and is used mainly for works relating to level crossings and road over and under bridges, whereas the Capital Fund is credited with appropriations made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways and finances asset-creating (capital) works out of the Railways' internal resources

e: The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge on fares for level crossing and road bridge works. The Capital Fund is credited from surplus and finances capital works from internal resources.

q: A work of passenger amenities is financed from the Development Fund of the Railways. An Accounts Officer proposes to classify the expenditure on the work under Major Head 3002, on the ground that the Development Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue. The correct position is that the expenditure is classified:

options.A: Under Major Head 5002, classified by Plan Heads, with the Development Fund shown as the source of finance in the allocation of the work
options.B: Under Major Head 3002, as proposed by the Accounts Officer
options.C: Under the Public Account of India, outside the Consolidated Fund
options.D: Under Major Head 3001, as a miscellaneous organisation expenditure

e: Works financed from Railway Funds are classified under Major Head 5002 by Plan Heads, with the fund such as the Development Fund shown as the source of finance in the allocation, not under Major Head 3002.

q: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account of the Central and State Governments, followed in the classification of accounts, is issued by the:

options.A: Railway Board
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance

e: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account for Central and State Governments is issued by the Controller General of Accounts in the Ministry of Finance.

q: On the day on which the Union Budget is presented to Parliament, a member seeks to raise a discussion on the Budget in the Lok Sabha on the same day. The correct position is that:

options.A: A general discussion on the Budget takes place on the day of its presentation itself
options.B: A discussion can be held on the day of presentation with the permission of the Finance Minister
options.C: No discussion on the Budget takes place in Parliament on the day on which it is presented
options.D: The Demands for Grants are voted on the day of presentation of the Budget

e: No discussion on the Budget takes place in Parliament on the day on which it is presented. The general discussion is held on a subsequent day fixed by the House.

q: A newly posted clerk treats the Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway as an office of the executive department, since it handles cash receipts and payments. The correct position is that the Cash & Pay Office functions as a part of the:

options.A: Executive department which incurs the expenditure
options.B: Traffic Accounts Office of another zonal railway
options.C: Reserve Bank of India

e: The Cash and Pay Office, which handles cash receipts and payments for the railway, functions as a part of the Accounts Department, not of the executive department.

q: A clerk in the Railway Board assumes that only the zonal railways render a monthly Account Current to the Railway Board. The correct position is that a monthly Account Current is also rendered by:

options.A: A production unit, such as the Integral Coach Factory, which is an independent accounting unit
options.B: Every division of a zonal railway, independently of the zonal railway
options.C: Every station of a zonal railway, independently of the division
options.D: The accredited bank, on behalf of the zonal railways

e: Besides zonal railways, a production unit such as the Integral Coach Factory, being an independent accounting unit, also renders a monthly Account Current to the Railway Board.

q: The working losses of the Strategic Lines maintained by the Railways for strategic (defence) considerations are, in the railway accounts:

options.A: Borne by the Railways out of their own earnings, without any reimbursement
options.B: Borne by General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways on strategic considerations
options.C: Met out of the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.D: Debited to the Capital Fund of the Railways

e: Working losses of Strategic Lines maintained for defence considerations are borne by General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways for those losses.

q: While linking the capital accounts of the Railways with the accounts of the Central Government, a clerk proposes to treat the Plan Heads of the railway classification as its Primary Units. The correct position is that, under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, the Plan Heads function as the:

options.A: Primary Units
options.C: Minor Heads

e: Under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, the Plan Heads of the railway classification function as the Minor Heads for linking railway capital accounts with Central Government accounts.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament, while examining the estimates of the Ministry of Railways, proposes to go into the merits of the policy underlying the estimates and to recommend its rejection. The correct position is that the Committee does NOT go into:

options.A: The form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament
options.B: Economies that can be effected in administration
options.C: Improvements in organisation and efficiency
options.D: The merits of the policy underlying the estimates, the policy itself being a matter for Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee can suggest economies and improvements in organisation and form of estimates, but it does not go into the merits of the policy underlying the estimates, policy being a matter for Parliament.

q: Sub-vouchers in support of small contingent payments made by a disbursing officer of a zonal railway are ordinarily:

options.A: Retained by the disbursing officer in his office and not forwarded to the Accounts Office
options.B: Forwarded to the Accounts Office along with every contingent bill
options.C: Sent to the Railway Board for post-audit
options.D: Destroyed immediately after the payment is made

e: Sub-vouchers for small contingent payments are ordinarily retained by the disbursing officer in his office and are not forwarded to the Accounts Office with the contingent bill.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement from the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?

options.A: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing year, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for the specified fiscal indicators
options.B: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year
options.C: Both statements set out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, the two being alternative names for the same document
options.D: Both statements are presented only in an election year, along with the Interim Budget

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators. The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets the strategic fiscal priorities for the ensuing year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Debt Service Fund from the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Debt Service Fund is credited with appropriations made from the revenues of the Railways to provide a cushion for meeting debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to the working expenses and finances renewals and replacements of assets
options.B: The Debt Service Fund is credited with the proceeds of market borrowings raised through IRFC, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited out of the surplus of the Railways
options.C: The Debt Service Fund finances renewals and replacements of over-aged assets, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund services the market borrowings of the Railways
options.D: Both funds are credited out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways at the close of the financial year

e: The Debt Service Fund is credited from railway revenues as a cushion for debt-service in lean years. The DRF is charged to working expenses and finances renewals and replacements of assets.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'AG Suspense' from 'PSB Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: AG Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for adjustments with State Governments
options.B: AG Suspense is operated only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas PSB Suspense is operated only by the production units
options.C: AG Suspense is operated for adjustments of transactions between the Railways and the State Governments/Accountants General, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, pending settlement or receipt of the bank's advice
options.D: Both heads are operated for transactions with the Reserve Bank of India pending its advice

e: AG Suspense is for adjustments between Railways and State Governments or Accountants General. PSB Suspense is for transactions with the accredited public sector bank pending settlement or bank advice.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Key to Budget Documents' from the 'Expenditure Profile'?

options.A: The Key to Budget Documents presents a snapshot of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, whereas the Expenditure Profile explains the terms used in the Budget documents
options.B: The Key to Budget Documents contains the detailed estimates of the Ministry of Railways, whereas the Expenditure Profile contains the recommendations of the Finance Commission
options.C: Both documents explain, clause by clause, the provisions contained in the Finance Bill
options.D: The Key to Budget Documents explains the various other Budget documents and the terms used in them, whereas the Expenditure Profile presents a snapshot (broad overview) of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise

e: The Key to Budget Documents explains the other Budget documents and the terms used in them. The Expenditure Profile gives a ministry-wise and scheme-wise snapshot of the pattern of total expenditure.

q: For a service of great magnitude whose character is so indefinite that the demand for it cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant, Parliament makes a grant which is often described as a 'blank cheque' to the Government. The grant so made is a:

options.A: Vote on Account
options.C: Exceptional Grant

e: A Vote of Credit under Article 116 is granted for a service of great magnitude or indefinite character that cannot be detailed in a normal Demand, and is therefore described as a blank cheque to the Government.

q: After a grant is voted by Parliament, a zonal railway distributes the amount among its divisions and other spending units so that expenditure can be incurred by them. This distribution of the voted grant among the spending units and offices is known as:

options.A: Budget Allotment
options.C: Re-appropriation

e: Distribution of a voted grant among divisions and spending units of a railway, so that they can incur expenditure, is known as Budget Allotment, distinct from Appropriation by Parliament.

q: A finance officer describes a figure as the aggregate capital invested in the Railways, forming the base of its capital structure, with reference to which the financial results of the Railways are assessed. The figure he is referring to is the:

options.A: Block Account
options.C: Capital-at-charge

e: Capital-at-charge is the aggregate capital invested in the Railways and forms the base of its capital structure, with reference to which its financial results and dividend liability are assessed.

q: On the last day allotted for the voting of the Demands for Grants, the Speaker puts all the outstanding Demands together to the vote of the Lok Sabha, whether they have been discussed or not. This practice is known as:

options.A: Guillotine
options.C: Vote on Account

e: On the last allotted day, the Speaker applies the Guillotine and puts all outstanding Demands for Grants together to the vote of the Lok Sabha, whether discussed or not.

q: A particular budget of the Railways is framed not independently but on the basis of the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works, and is for that reason described as a 'derived' budget. The budget so described is the:

options.A: Earnings Budget
options.C: Revenue Budget

e: The Stores Budget is a derived budget, framed on the basis of the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works, rather than independently.

q: A clerk preparing the Budget papers for the year 2019-20 proposes to continue showing the expenditure of the Government under the two categories of 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan'. The correct position is that this distinction in the Government Budget was discontinued with effect from the financial year:
e: The distinction between Plan and Non-Plan expenditure in the Government Budget was discontinued with effect from the financial year 2017-18.

q: A parliamentary committee consisting of twenty-two members — fifteen drawn from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha — takes up for examination the reports and accounts of the railway public sector undertakings, together with the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on them. The committee so described is the:

options.A: Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Committee on Public Undertakings
options.D: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: The committee of 22 members, 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha, examining public undertakings and CAG reports on them, is the Committee on Public Undertakings.

q: While framing the estimates of a Ministry, the related receipts are not deducted from the expenditure, and the estimates are presented in full, without any netting off. The principle of Government budgeting followed in doing so is:

options.A: Gross budgeting
options.C: Unity of the Budget

e: Showing estimates in full without deducting related receipts is the principle of gross budgeting. Demands are presented gross, with recoveries shown separately as deduct entries.

q: A consignment is booked at a station of one zonal railway for a destination on another railway, and the freight is collected by the booking railway. In the apportionment of earnings, these through-traffic earnings are initially brought to account in full by:

options.A: The Railway Board, which thereafter divides them among the railways concerned
options.B: The railway on which the traffic originates, that is, the collecting railway, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned
options.C: The railway at which the traffic terminates
options.D: The Traffic Accounts Office of the destination railway alone

e: Through-traffic earnings are initially brought to account in full by the originating or collecting railway where the traffic is booked, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned by apportionment.

q: In the classification of a capital work financed from the Development Fund, a clerk proposes to indicate the source of finance as the Plan Head of the work. The correct position is that the source from which a work is financed (Capital, DRF, Development Fund, RRSK etc.) is indicated in its classification as its:

options.A: Primary Unit
options.C: Allocation

e: The source from which a work is financed, such as Capital, DRF, Development Fund or RRSK, is indicated in its classification as its Allocation, distinct from the Plan Head of the work.

q: Apart from recommending the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy recommended the setting up of an independent regulator for the Railways. The regulator so recommended is the:

options.A: Rail Development Authority
options.C: Railway Claims Tribunal

e: Apart from Budget merger, the Bibek Debroy Committee recommended an independent regulator for the Railways, namely the Rail Development Authority.

q: Midway through a financial year, it is found that the amount of a grant voted by Parliament needs to be increased. The increase in the amount of the grant can be effected only by:

options.A: An order of the Railway Board issued with the concurrence of the Financial Commissioner
options.B: Re-appropriation of savings available under another grant
options.C: An order of the Ministry of Finance issued under the General Financial Rules
options.D: A Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament

e: An increase in the amount of a grant already voted can be effected only by a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament. Re-appropriation can only move savings within the same grant.

q: The Demands for Grants having been voted and the Appropriation Bill having been passed by both Houses of Parliament, the Bill becomes the Appropriation Act on receiving the assent of:

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: After both Houses pass the Appropriation Bill, it becomes the Appropriation Act on receiving the assent of the President, authorising withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.

q: At the end of a month, a station renders to the Traffic Accounts Office a statement accounting for all its traffic transactions of the month and showing the balance due from the station. The statement so rendered is the:

options.A: Traffic Book
options.C: Station Balance Sheet

e: The monthly statement rendered by a station to the Traffic Accounts Office accounting for all its traffic transactions and showing the balance due from the station is the Station Balance Sheet.

q: In his Budget Speech, the Finance Minister first gives an overview of the economy and announces the major policies of the Government, before turning to the other part of the speech. The part of the Budget Speech in which this overview and the major policy announcements are given is:

options.A: Part A
options.C: Part C

e: Part A of the Budget Speech gives the overview of the economy and the major policy announcements of the Government. Part B deals with the tax proposals.

q: An Accounts Officer proposes that a separate appropriation by Parliament must be obtained before any amount can be withdrawn from the accumulated balance of the Depreciation Reserve Fund of a zonal railway. The correct position in this regard is that:

options.A: A separate appropriation by Parliament is required for every withdrawal from the Fund
options.B: No such separate appropriation is required, the balances of the Railway Funds being held in the Public Account of India and not lapsing at the close of the financial year
options.C: A withdrawal can be made only with the prior sanction of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: No withdrawal can be made at all, since the balance of the Fund lapses at the close of the financial year

e: Balances of Railway Funds are held in the Public Account of India and do not lapse at the close of the year, so no separate appropriation by Parliament is required for withdrawal from the accumulated DRF balance.

q: At the close of a financial year, balances are outstanding under certain suspense and remittance heads of a zonal railway, pending clearance. The correct treatment of these outstanding balances is that they:

options.A: Lapse to the Government at the close of the year
options.B: Are written off automatically at the close of the year
options.C: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund
options.D: Are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance

e: Outstanding balances under suspense and remittance heads do not lapse or get written off at the close of the year. They are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance.

q: Under the door-step banking arrangement, the accredited bank collects the earnings of stations and deposits them in the Railways' current account maintained for the purpose. The account into which the collections are so deposited is styled the:

options.A: Rail Shakti Account
options.C: Rail Setu Account

e: Under door-step banking, station earnings collected by the accredited bank are deposited in the Railways current account styled the Rail Shakti Account.

q: A zonal railway expects to receive its budget allotment for a financial year as soon as the Budget is presented to Parliament. Ordinarily, the budget allotment for the year is communicated by the Railway Board to the zonal railways:

options.A: Before the presentation of the Budget in Parliament
options.B: Along with the Revised Estimates in September
options.C: After the Appropriation Act for the year has been passed
options.D: Only at the Final Modification stage in January

e: The budget allotment for a year is ordinarily communicated by the Railway Board to zonal railways after the Appropriation Act for the year has been passed.

q: The estimates of earnings of a zonal railway are first framed by its operating and commercial departments. Before these estimates are adopted in the Budget, they are scrutinised by the:

options.A: Railway Board's Traffic Directorate alone, without any accounts scrutiny
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Earnings estimates first framed by operating and commercial departments are scrutinised by the Accounts Department before they are adopted in the Budget.

q: Under exchequer control, the expenditure of the Ministries and Departments of the Government during the year is regulated through:

options.A: Budget proportions fixed by the Railway Board
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year
options.D: Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans

e: Under exchequer control, departmental expenditure during the year is regulated through Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans agreed with the Ministry of Finance.

q: The Operating Ratio of a zonal railway for a year is 90 per cent and its net revenue (surplus) for the year is Rs 550 crore. The gross earnings of the railway for the year are:

options.A: Rs 5,500 crore
options.C: Rs 6,100 crore

e: With Operating Ratio 90 per cent, surplus is 10 per cent of gross earnings. So gross earnings = Rs 550 crore / 0.10 = Rs 5,500 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 11,50,000 crore and its primary deficit for the year is Rs 7,00,000 crore. The interest payments of the Government during the year are:

options.A: Rs 18,50,000 crore
options.C: Rs 7,00,000 crore

e: Interest payments = fiscal deficit - primary deficit = Rs 11,50,000 crore - Rs 7,00,000 crore = Rs 4,50,000 crore.

q: The sanctioned amount of an imprest held by an officer is Rs 18,000. At a surprise check, the cash in hand with the holder is Rs 5,200. The amount of the paid vouchers held by him in support of the expenditure incurred out of the imprest, and not yet recouped, is:
e: Paid vouchers not yet recouped = sanctioned imprest - cash in hand = Rs 18,000 - Rs 5,200 = Rs 12,800.

q: The annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund on account of an asset of the Railways, assessed with reference to the original cost of the asset and its prescribed (codal) life, amounts to Rs 15,000, the codal life of the asset being 25 years. The original cost of the asset is:
e: Original cost = annual DRF appropriation x codal life = Rs 15,000 x 25 = Rs 3,75,000.

q: The total lease charges payable by the Railways to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation for a year are Rs 13,200 crore, of which the capital (principal) component is Rs 7,800 crore. The interest (finance charge) component of the lease charges for the year is:

options.A: Rs 7,800 crore
options.C: Rs 4,600 crore

e: Interest component = total lease charges - capital component = Rs 13,200 crore - Rs 7,800 crore = Rs 5,400 crore.
